safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not explicitly state no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting an explicit statement that there is no evidence of cellulitis can reduce clarity for downstream clinicians reviewing the note, potentially prompting unnecessary additional monitoring or empiric antibiotics if the local reaction is misinterpreted. However, the encounter context still emphasizes localized reaction and provides infection warning signs, limiting the likelihood of significant harm.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly asserting the patient has no current medications can cause medication-reconciliation errors, including missed drug–drug interactions, contraindications, or duplications when advising antihistamines. While many patients will tolerate OTC antihistamines, an inaccurate med list can lead to avoidable adverse effects or suboptimal decisions.
